  "research_question": "How does stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) affect mouse navigation performance across five metrics: Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": ["Use one-way ANOVA for each response variable with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor, comparing means across the five groups. For Success (binary), use logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as predictor instead of standard ANOVA."],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": ["Check normality of residuals (QQ-plots, Shapiro-Wilk test) for continuous variables: Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD", "Check homogeneity of variances (Levene's test) for continuous variables", "Assess independence of observations (design-based assumption)", "For logistic regression (Success), check linearity and overdispersion"],
  "posthoc_plan": ["If omnibus ANOVA is significant (p<0.05), perform Tukey HSD for pairwise comparisons. For logistic regression (Success), use pairwise comparisons with adjusted p-values (e.g., Bonferroni) if overall model is significant"],
  "expected_findings": ["Sham condition will show worst performance: highest Time-to-Target (4.68s), lowest Success (0.27), lowest Path Efficiency (0.31), lowest Average Speed (10.74), lowest AD (0.24)", "Active stimulation paradigms (Combined, Bright Visual Only) will show best performance: lower Time-to-Target (~2.56-2.61s), higher Success (~0.78), higher Path Efficiency (~0.50), higher Average Speed (~12.68-12.83), higher AD (~0.39-0.40)", "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only will show intermediate performance between Sham and active conditions"],
  "limitations": ["Uneven group sizes: Combined has 48,846 observations while Bright Visual Only has only 3,323, Sham has 3,505", "Potential violation of normality assumption for variables with skewed distributions (e.g., Path Efficiency min=0.0009, max=29.82)", "Success is binary (0/1), requiring logistic regression instead of standard ANOVA", "No information about within-mouse correlations or random effects structure"],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Add mouse as random effect in mixed-effects models (e.g., LMM for continuous variables, GLMM for Success) to account for repeated measures and individual differences"
}
